## 1. Executive summary

The two repositories solve **different halves** of the same problem, and your base is currently missing pieces of both halves.

- **Matt Pocock's repo is a front-of-funnel and design-quality system.** Its centre of gravity is *before* code exists: relentless interviewing (`grilling`), a shared domain language that persists across sessions (`CONTEXT.md` + ADRs), a deep-module design vocabulary, and tracker-native task graphs. Skills are small (~80 lines), composable, explicitly hackable, and split by *who can invoke them*. Its execution layer is deliberately thin — `implement` is seven lines.
- **Superpowers is a back-of-funnel execution and enforcement system.** Its centre of gravity is *after* the design is agreed: an approval hard-gate, executable plans with no placeholders, and a 568-line controller loop that dispatches a fresh subagent per task, gates each one with a two-verdict review, runs a bounded fix loop with model escalation, and keeps a ledger that survives compaction. It has no domain-language layer and almost no architecture vocabulary.

Your base sits in a third position: **you have the deepest domain-specific library knowledge of the three** (Kafka + outbox + db-core + Spring Boot standards, ~10,800 reference lines that neither reference repo could produce), plus a genuinely novel upstream-drift mechanism (`sync-dependent-skills`) and a structural self-audit (`my-skills-audit`) that neither repo has.

What you're missing is the **top and the bottom of the funnel**:

|                       | You have                                 | You're missing                                                                                                                      |
| --------------------- | ---------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| **Elicitation**       | —                                        | Any interview/grilling stage. Nothing asks you what you actually want before drafting.                                              |
| **Persistent memory** | —                                        | `CONTEXT.md` glossary, ADR convention, on-disk spec/plan artifacts. Everything is re-derived per session or lives remotely in Jira. |
| **Ticketing**         | `to-jira-issues` (strong Jira mechanics) | Split into spec/breakdown/evolve; per-ticket interface contracts.                                                                   |
| **Planning**          | —                                        | Any plan artifact between ticket and code.                                                                                          |
| **Execution**         | `implement-issue` (good token instincts) | Subagent delegation, ledger, worktrees, model tiers, bounded fix loop, escalation contract.                                         |
| **Verification**      | `check-diagnostics`                      | An evidence-before-claims gate.                                                                                                     |
| **Review**            | `code-review` (2 axes, well engineered)  | Correctness axis, severity taxonomy, verdict, review-package file.                                                                  |
| **Debugging**         | —                                        | Nothing. No root-cause discipline among 32 skills.                                                                                  |
| **Design**            | Standards skills                         | Deep-module vocabulary; seam selection across your four testing skills.                                                             |
| **Meta**              | `my-skills-audit` (ahead of both)        | Router skill, authoring discipline, behavioural evals, invocation hygiene.                                                          |

**The three highest-leverage moves, in order:**

1. **Add a grilling stage and a `CONTEXT.md` glossary.** Both reference repos independently identify requirement misalignment as the #1 failure mode, and both put an interview first. Matt calls grilling his most popular skill; Superpowers makes design approval a hard gate that no path can skip. You currently go from a Jira reference straight to a drafted issue body. This is the single biggest correctness gap.
2. **Insert a plan artifact and a subagent execution loop between ticket and code.** Your `implement-issue` runs everything in one context window with no resume point. Superpowers' measured cost breakdown shows the controller's resident context is the largest single line item — and their fix (fresh subagent per task, artifacts handed over as file paths, explicit model tiers) is directly portable. This is the biggest cost *and* scale win.
3. **Do the invocation-hygiene sweep.** 31 of your 32 skills are model-invocable, so 31 descriptions — several over 120 words — sit in resident context on every turn of every session. Matt's user-invoked/model-invoked split costs nothing to adopt and reclaims real budget immediately.

## 2. Matt Pocock's skills: workflow map

### The main flow: idea → ship

```
                       ┌─────────────────────────────────────┐
                       │  /setup-matt-pocock-skills          │  run once per repo
                       │  (issue tracker, labels, doc paths) │
                       └─────────────────────────────────────┘
                                        │
   ┌────────────────────────────────────▼─────────────────────────────────────┐
   │ 1.  /grill-with-docs      = /grilling  +  /domain-modeling               │
   │     relentless interview, rounds over a design tree,                     │
   │     writing CONTEXT.md glossary + ADRs inline as decisions land          │
   └────────────────────────────────────┬─────────────────────────────────────┘
                                        │
                    ┌───────────────────┴───────────────────┐
                    │ Can every question be settled in      │
                    │ conversation?                          │
                    └───────┬───────────────────────┬────────┘
                        no  │                       │ yes
              ┌─────────────▼──────────┐            │
              │ /handoff → /prototype  │            │
              │ → /handoff back        │            │
              │ (throwaway code        │            │
              │  answers one question) │            │
              └─────────────┬──────────┘            │
                            └───────────┬───────────┘
                                        │
                    ┌───────────────────┴───────────────────┐
                    │ Multi-session build?                   │
                    └───────┬───────────────────────┬────────┘
                       yes  │                       │ no
       ┌──────────────────▼─────────────┐           │
       │ /to-spec    (synthesise, no    │           │
       │              re-interview)     │           │
       │      ▼                         │           │
       │ /to-tickets (tracer-bullet     │           │
       │   vertical slices + blocking   │           │
       │   edges → tracker)             │           │
       └──────────────────┬─────────────┘           │
                          │  one /implement per ticket,
                          │  /clear between each
                          └─────────────┬───────────┘
                                        ▼
                       ┌────────────────────────────────┐
                       │ /implement                     │
                       │   ├─ drives /tdd internally    │
                       │   │   (one red-green slice     │
                       │   │    at a time, at pre-      │
                       │   │    agreed seams)           │
                       │   └─ closes with /code-review  │
                       │       (Standards ‖ Spec)       │
                       │       then commits             │
                       └────────────────────────────────┘
```

**Context hygiene rule:** steps 1–3 stay in *one unbroken context window* (no compact, no clear until after `/to-tickets`) so grilling, spec, and tickets all build on the same primary source. Each `/implement` then starts fresh from its ticket. The bound is the "smart zone" (~150k tokens) within which the model still reasons sharply.

### On-ramps (situations that generate work, then merge onto the main flow)

| On-ramp                                   | Skill                                                                                                                                                                           | Merges in at                                                                             |
| ----------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Bugs/requests piling up from other people | `/triage` — state machine of roles (`needs-triage` → `needs-info` / `ready-for-agent` / `ready-for-human` / `wontfix`), verifies the claim before grilling, writes agent briefs | `/implement`                                                                             |
| Something's broken                        | `/diagnosing-bugs` — six gated phases, refuses to theorise without a tight red-capable loop                                                                                     | its own fix, or `/improve-codebase-architecture` if the finding is "no good seam exists" |
| Effort too big for one session            | `/wayfinder` — charts a shared map of **decision** tickets on the tracker, resolves one per session until the fog clears                                                        | `/to-spec`                                                                               |
| Codebase entropy                          | `/improve-codebase-architecture` — periodic survey for deepening opportunities, HTML report, then grills the one you pick                                                       | `/grill-with-docs`                                                                       |

### Layers underneath

Two model-invoked **vocabulary** skills run beneath everything, each the single source of truth for its language:

- `domain-modeling` — the project's *domain* language (`CONTEXT.md`, ADRs)
- `codebase-design` — the *deep-module* language (module, interface, depth, seam, adapter, leverage, locality)

And two meta layers: `ask-matt` (router over user-invoked skills; a "router that lies" if it goes stale) and `writing-for-agents` (how to write anything an agent consumes).

### The organising invariant

Every skill is **exactly one of**:

- **User-invoked** (`disable-model-invocation: true`): reachable only by a human typing its name. Zero context load. Description is human-facing. *Its job is to orchestrate.*
- **Model-invoked**: reachable by model or human. Permanent context load in exchange for auto-discovery. Description is model-facing with rich trigger phrasing. *Its job is to hold reusable discipline.*

A user-invoked skill may invoke model-invoked skills; it can **never** reach another user-invoked skill. Dependencies are expressed as an explicit `Call the Skill tool with "grilling"`, never as a cross-folder `../other/FILE.md` link.

### The organising invariant

**Behavioural enforcement over description.** Almost every skill carries the same four devices:

1. An **Iron Law** stated as a code block.
2. A **Red Flags** table: the rationalizing *thought* in the left column, the *reality* in the right.
3. A **Common Rationalizations** table (same shape, aimed at excuses rather than thoughts).
4. "**Violating the letter of the rules is violating the spirit of the rules.**"

These are tuned against a real eval harness (`drill`, driving tmux sessions with an LLM verifier). The repo explicitly refuses "compliance" PRs that reword skills toward Anthropic's published style without eval evidence — the phrasing *is* the product.

## 4. Skill-by-skill breakdown

### 4a. Matt Pocock — engineering

| Skill                             | Invocation | Steps / rules, condensed                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                     |
| --------------------------------- | ---------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| **grilling**                      | model      | 1. Map the request as a **design tree**. 2. The **frontier** = every decision whose prerequisites are settled. 3. Ask the *whole frontier* in one round; number each question; **give your recommended answer** to each. 4. Wait for answers. 5. Recompute the frontier; repeat. Rules: **facts are the agent's job** (dispatch a subagent, never ask the user what you could look up); **decisions are the user's**; a question depending on an open question belongs to a later round; done when the frontier is empty; don't act until the user confirms shared understanding.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            |
| **grill-with-docs**               | user       | One line: `Call the Skill tool twice, for "grilling" and "domain-modeling"`. (A composition, not a skill.)                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                   |
| **domain-modeling**               | model      | Active discipline only (reading `CONTEXT.md` is *not* this skill). 1. Challenge terms that conflict with the glossary, immediately. 2. Sharpen fuzzy/overloaded terms into one canonical term. 3. Stress-test relationships with invented edge-case scenarios. 4. Cross-reference claims against the code; surface contradictions. 5. Update `CONTEXT.md` **inline**, never batched. 6. Offer an ADR only when *all three* hold: hard to reverse, surprising without context, result of a real trade-off. `CONTEXT.md` is a glossary and nothing else.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       |
| **to-spec**                       | user       | **Do NOT interview** — synthesise what's already known. 1. Explore repo; use glossary vocabulary; respect ADRs. 2. **Sketch the test seams; prefer existing; use the highest possible; fewest possible, ideally one; confirm with the user.** 3. Write spec (Problem / Solution / *long* numbered User Stories / Implementation Decisions / Testing Decisions / Out of Scope / Notes), publish to tracker, label `ready-for-agent`. No file paths or code snippets (they go stale) — except a prototype-derived snippet that encodes a decision more precisely than prose.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                   |
| **to-tickets**                    | user       | 1. Gather context (fetch any referenced spec/issue in full). 2. Explore codebase; look for **prefactoring** ("make the change easy, then make the easy change") — becomes its own first ticket. 3. Draft **tracer bullets**: narrow but *complete* path through every layer; demoable alone; fits one fresh context window; explicit **blocking edges**. 4. **Exception — wide refactors**: sequence expand → migrate batches → contract, never a forced tracer bullet. 5. Quiz the user (granularity? edges correct? merge/split?) until approved. 6. Publish blockers-first so edges can reference real ids; native blocking links where the tracker has them. Work the **frontier**. Never modify the parent issue.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       |
| **implement**                     | user       | Seven lines: implement per spec/tickets; use `/tdd` at pre-agreed seams; typecheck often, single test files often, full suite once at the end; `/code-review`; commit.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       |
| **tdd**                           | model      | *What a good test is*: verifies behaviour through public interfaces; reads like a specification. **Seams**: the public boundary you test at; tests live at seams, never against internals; **test only at pre-agreed seams, confirmed with the user before any test is written**; highest seam possible; fewest seams. Anti-patterns: **implementation-coupled** (tell: breaks on refactor without behaviour change); **tautological** (assertion recomputes the expected value the way the code does — expected values must come from an independent source of truth); **horizontal slicing** (all tests then all implementation). Rules: red before green; one slice at a time; **refactoring is not part of the loop — it belongs to review**.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            |
| **code-review**                   | model      | Two axes in **parallel sub-agents** so neither pollutes the other. 1. Pin the fixed point; `git diff <fp>...HEAD` (three-dot); verify the ref resolves and the diff is non-empty *before* dispatching. 2. Find the spec (commit-message issue refs → user arg → spec file → ask). 3. Standards sources = repo docs **plus a fixed 12-smell Fowler baseline** (Mysterious Name, Duplicated Code, Feature Envy, Data Clumps, Primitive Obsession, Repeated Switches, Shotgun Surgery, Divergent Change, Speculative Generality, Message Chains, Middle Man, Refused Bequest), each *what it is → how to fix*. Repo docs override the baseline; baseline smells are always judgement calls; skip anything tooling enforces. 4. Dispatch both, 400 words each. 5. Aggregate verbatim under `## Standards` / `## Spec` — **never merge or rerank**, since one axis masking the other is exactly what the split prevents.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          |
| **diagnosing-bugs**               | model      | **Phase 1 is the skill; everything else is mechanical.** Build a **tight** pass/fail loop that goes **red on this bug**. Ten ways, in order: failing test → curl script → CLI+fixture diff → headless browser → replay a captured trace → throwaway harness → property/fuzz loop → bisection harness → differential loop → HITL bash script (last resort). Then *tighten* it: faster, sharper signal, more deterministic. Non-deterministic bugs: raise the **reproduction rate**, don't chase a clean repro. Completion criterion: **one named command you have already run**, red-capable / deterministic / fast / agent-runnable. "If you catch yourself reading code to build a theory before this command exists, stop." Phase 2 reproduce **and minimise** (cut one element at a time until every remaining element is load-bearing). Phase 3: **3–5 ranked falsifiable hypotheses** before testing any, each stating its prediction; show the list to the user. Phase 4: one probe per prediction, one variable at a time; debugger > targeted logs > never "log everything and grep"; **tag every debug log `[DEBUG-a4f2]`** so cleanup is one grep; perf regressions measure first. Phase 5: regression test before the fix, **but only if a correct seam exists** — if none does, *that is itself the finding*. Phase 6: six-item cleanup checklist; the winning hypothesis goes in the commit message. Redact every secret first. |
| **codebase-design**               | model      | Design **deep modules**: a lot of behaviour behind a small interface at a clean seam. Glossary used *exactly*: **Module** (scale-agnostic), **Interface** (everything a caller must know — invariants, ordering, error modes, perf, not just the signature), **Implementation**, **Depth** (leverage at the interface), **Seam** (Feathers: alter behaviour without editing in that place), **Adapter** (role, not substance), **Leverage** (callers), **Locality** (maintainers). Principles: depth is a property of the *interface*; **the deletion test** (delete it — does complexity vanish or reappear across N callers?); **the interface is the test surface**; **one adapter = hypothetical seam, two = real one**. `DEEPENING.md`: four dependency categories (in-process / local-substitutable / remote-but-owned → port+adapter / true external → mock) determine how the deepened module is tested; **replace, don't layer** (delete the old shallow-module unit tests). `DESIGN-IT-TWICE.md`: spawn 3+ parallel sub-agents, each with a *different* constraint (minimise the interface / maximise flexibility / optimise the common caller / ports-and-adapters), compare on depth, locality, seam placement, then be opinionated.                                                                                                                                                                                             |
| **improve-codebase-architecture** | user       | 1. **Scope before you scan (YAGNI)** — walk `git log` for hot spots; weight recently-changed code. 2. Sub-agent walks the codebase noting *friction*, not heuristics; apply the deletion test. 3. Self-contained HTML report in `$TMPDIR` (Tailwind + Mermaid CDN), one card per candidate with before/after diagram and a `Strong`/`Worth exploring`/`Speculative` badge; **do not propose interfaces yet**. 4. User picks one → grilling loop, with `CONTEXT.md`/ADR side effects inline.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  |
| **triage**                        | user       | State machine: 2 category roles (`bug`/`enhancement`) + 5 state roles (`needs-triage`, `needs-info`, `ready-for-agent`, `ready-for-human`, `wontfix`). Every posted comment starts with an AI-generated disclaimer. Per issue: gather context → run a **redundancy check** (search by domain concept, not the request's wording) and a **prior-rejection check** (`.out-of-scope/*.md`) → recommend and wait → **verify the claim** (reproduce the bug / check the diff does what it claims) → grill if needed → apply outcome. "A PR is an issue with attached code." Triage is only for issues *you didn't create*.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        |
| **wayfinder**                     | user       | For efforts too big for one session. **Name the destination first** (it fixes the scope). The **map** is one tracker issue labelled `wayfinder:map`, an *index* not a store. Children are **decision tickets** (questions whose resolution is a decision, not slices to execute) sized to one ~100k session, each typed `research` (AFK) / `prototype` / `grilling` / `task`. Native blocking links render the **frontier** visually. **Claim by assigning yourself before any work.** **Fog of war**: don't chart what you can't see — `## Not yet specified` holds the dim view; the test is whether you can *state* the question now, not answer it. `## Out of scope` is a scoping act, never graduates. **Plan, don't do.** Never resolve more than one ticket per session (research excepted).                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                         |
| **prototype**                     | model      | Throwaway code that answers *one* design question. Throwaway is a constraint on how it's written, not a promise to delete it: the prototype is kept as a **primary source** on a `prototype/<name>` branch off main, linked from the implementation issue.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                   |
| **research**                      | model      | Background agent; **primary sources only** (official docs, source, specs, first-party APIs — never a secondary write-up); one cited Markdown file, saved to the repo's existing convention.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  |
| **resolving-merge-conflicts**     | model      | Hunk by hunk, resolving by **intent traced to each side's primary source**, then finish the operation. **Never `--abort`.**                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  |
| **wizard**                        | model      | Generates an interactive bash script for steps only a human can take (provisioning, credentials, CI secrets, third-party dashboards, one-off cutovers) so the procedure stops being re-explained every time.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                 |
| **setup-matt-pocock-skills**      | user       | Run once per repo: choose issue tracker, triage label vocabulary, doc locations. Every downstream skill says "the tracker should have been provided to you; if not, tell the user to run `/setup-…`".                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        |
| **ask-matt**                      | user       | The router. Maps the main flow, the three on-ramps, codebase health, the two vocabulary layers, standalone skills, and the precondition. Carries `PHASE-BOUNDARIES.md`.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      |

### 4b. Matt Pocock — productivity (selected)

| Skill                   | Steps / rules, condensed                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                             |
| ----------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| **writing-for-agents**  | The **two loads**: *context load* (always-resident tokens — descriptions, `AGENTS.md` lines) vs *cognitive load* (the human remembering what exists; "not a cost to minimise: it is the price of human agency"). The **information hierarchy** ladder: (1) in-file step, (2) in-file reference, (3) disclosed reference behind a pointer. **Progressive disclosure** = moving down the ladder; the test is **branching** — inline what every branch needs, disclose what only some branches reach. **Co-location** within a file. **Sprawl** as the failure mode. **Completion criteria** have two properties: *clarity* (vague bounds invite premature completion) and *demand* (how much they require, which drives latent legwork). **Leading words**: a compact pretrained concept (*tight*, *red*, *tracer bullet*, *fog of war*) repeated as a token, never as a sentence — it anchors execution in the body and invocation in the pointer; coining your own costs you the priors. **Negation is the failure mode beside it**: steering by prohibition drags the forbidden behaviour into context and makes it *more* available; prompt the positive. **Pruning**: single source of truth; the environment is a source of truth too (a doc restating `package.json` is a *cache* that goes stale); check every line for *relevance*; hunt **no-ops** (an instruction the model already obeys by default) sentence by sentence and delete the whole sentence; the default fate without pruning is **sediment**. |
| **PHASE-BOUNDARIES.md** | Five options at a boundary, first *yes* wins: (1) **Continue** — rule it out first; costs nothing, loses nothing; yes if the next phase needs this one as a *primary source*, or the smart zone still fits. (2) **`/clear`** if the context is irrelevant to what's next (cheapest move; getting it wrong is one-way — you lose the *why*). (3) **`/handoff`** only for a new harness, new directory, a colleague, or forking a side task mid-phase; what it buys is *portability*. (4) **Subagent** if the task can run AFK. (5) **`/compact`** — the default, deliberately at the *bottom*. Every move except Continue turns a primary source into a lossy secondary one. Make the decision **at** a boundary, never mid-phase.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    |
| **handoff**             | Portable markdown to the OS temp dir (not the workspace). Includes a "suggested skills" section. **Never duplicate what a pointer can reach** (specs, plans, ADRs, issues, commits, diffs). Redact secrets.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          |
| **wait-what**           | Fire the moment a message doesn't land; re-pitch with the missing context, in plain English, using `CONTEXT.md` vocabulary.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          |
| **to-questionnaire**    | Inverse of grilling: interviews you about the *send* (who it's for, what you need back), not the subject.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            |

### 4c. Superpowers

| Skill                                                        | Steps / rules, condensed                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              |
| ------------------------------------------------------------ | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| **using-superpowers**                                        | The bootstrap, injected at session start and after compaction. "If you think there is even a 1% chance a skill might apply, you ABSOLUTELY MUST invoke it." Invoke **before any response** including clarifying questions or exploring the codebase. Announce "Using [skill] to [purpose]"; a checklist becomes one todo per item. Process skills precede implementation skills. 12-row Red Flags table ("This is just a simple question" → "Questions are tasks"; "Let me explore the codebase first" → "Skills tell you HOW to explore"; "I remember this skill" → "Skills evolve. Read the current version"). User instructions outrank skills.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    |
| **brainstorming**                                            | See the map above. Key devices: **classify out loud** so the human can override; `<HARD-GATE>` — no implementation action of any kind before stated intent is approved, on *every* path; **what scales with simplicity is the artifact, never the approval**; the **one-way ratchet** (hidden complexity upgrades the path mid-task, nothing downgrades); "bounded measures the repo, not your familiarity — a new project has no existing flow, so it is architectural"; questions one per message; propose 2–3 approaches lead-with-recommendation; **YAGNI ruthlessly**; design presented in sections with approval after each; spec self-review (placeholder scan / internal consistency / scope / ambiguity) then a **user review gate**; terminal states are path-bound (architectural → *only* `writing-plans`).                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                               |
| **writing-plans**                                            | Write for "a skilled developer who knows almost nothing about our toolset or domain and doesn't know good test design." **File Structure** section first (decomposition decisions get locked in here). **Task right-sizing**: "the smallest unit that carries its own test cycle and is worth a fresh reviewer's gate — fold setup/config/scaffolding/docs into the task whose deliverable needs them; split only where a reviewer could meaningfully reject one task while approving its neighbour." Header carries **Spec path** and **`## Global Constraints`** (exact values verbatim). Per task: **Files** (exact paths + line ranges), **Interfaces** (consumes / produces, exact signatures — "a task's implementer sees only their own task; this block is how they learn the names and types neighbouring tasks use"), then 2–5-minute steps *containing real code*. **No Placeholders** listed as *plan failures*, including "Similar to Task N" (repeat the code; tasks are read out of order). Self-review: spec coverage / placeholder scan / **type consistency across tasks**.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                         |
| **subagent-driven-development**                              | See the map. Beyond that: **"Rulings, not stalls"** — a running plan does not wait on a human; decide conflicts, ambiguities, plan defects, and record `Ruling: <what> — <why> — <what it costs if wrong>`. Exactly four things stop you: irreversible/destructive ops, security-sensitive actions, side effects outside the worktree (merge, push to shared, publish), and a plan so broken every path is a guess. **Model Selection**: least powerful model that can do the role; "**always specify the model explicitly** — an omitted model inherits your session's model, which silently defeats this section"; **turn count beats token price** (cheap models take 2-3× the turns on multi-step work, costing more overall) so mid-tier is the *floor* for reviewers and prose-driven implementers, cheapest tier only when the plan text contains the code to transcribe; escalate one tier at fix rounds 4-5. **Batch small same-shape work** into one dispatch. "Everything you paste into a dispatch prompt stays resident for the rest of the session — hand artifacts over as **files**." Anti-patterns called out by name: pasting accumulated prior-task summaries (a real session hit 42k chars, 99% pasted history); workers spawning their own reviewers (a duplicate review seat per task); `HEAD~1` as the review base (silently drops all but the last commit); **pre-judging findings** ("if the prompt contains 'do not flag' — stop, you are sparing yourself a review loop"). |
| **test-driven-development**                                  | **Iron Law: NO PRODUCTION CODE WITHOUT A FAILING TEST FIRST.** Wrote code first? **Delete it** — don't keep it as reference, don't adapt it, don't look at it. Verify RED is *mandatory*: test must **fail, not error**, and fail because the feature is missing, not because of a typo; a test that passes means you're testing existing behaviour. GREEN = simplest code, nothing more. Output must be **pristine** (warnings are failures). 10-row rationalization table — the best entries argue *why*: "tests written after pass immediately, which proves nothing"; "tests-after answer *what does this do*, tests-first answer *what should this do*"; "sunk cost — that time is already spent either way." 13-item Red Flags list, all resolving to "delete code, start over." 8-item verification checklist.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                 |
| **verification-before-completion**                           | **Iron Law: NO COMPLETION CLAIMS WITHOUT FRESH VERIFICATION EVIDENCE.** "If you haven't run the verification command *in this message*, you cannot claim it passes." The **gate function**: identify the command → run it FULL and fresh → read full output, exit code, failure count → does it confirm the claim → only then speak. Claim→requires→not-sufficient table (`Build succeeds` requires exit 0, *not* "linter passed"; `Agent completed` requires a VCS diff, *not* the agent's own success report; `Requirements met` requires a line-by-line checklist, *not* passing tests). Red flags include "should / probably / seems to" and **any expression of satisfaction before verification** ("Great!", "Perfect!", "Done!"). Regression tests need the full red-green cycle verified: write → pass → **revert the fix** → must fail → restore → pass.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                     |
| **systematic-debugging**                                     | **Iron Law: NO FIXES WITHOUT ROOT CAUSE INVESTIGATION FIRST.** Phase 1: read errors completely, reproduce consistently, check recent changes, **instrument every component boundary and run once to find *where* it breaks** before suspecting *what*, trace data flow backward to the source. Phase 2: find working examples in the same codebase, read reference implementations *completely*, list **every** difference however small. Phase 3: one hypothesis stated explicitly, smallest possible test, one variable; didn't work ⇒ **new** hypothesis, don't stack fixes. Phase 4: failing test first, single fix, no "while I'm here"; **≥3 failed fixes ⇒ stop and question the architecture** — "this is NOT a failed hypothesis, this is a wrong architecture."                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                             |
| **requesting-code-review**                                   | Mandatory after each SDD task, after a major feature, before merge. Get BASE/HEAD SHAs, dispatch a reviewer with the `code-reviewer.md` template. Rationalization: "I'll just review the diff myself" → "you're the coordinator; reviewing inline burns the context window you need to keep driving the work." Reviewer template returns **Strengths → Issues (Critical / Important / Minor, each with file:line, what's wrong, why it matters, how to fix) → Recommendations → Assessment (Ready to merge? Yes / No / With fixes + reasoning)**. Checks five families: plan alignment, code quality, architecture, testing (real behaviour vs mocks), **production readiness** (migration strategy, backward compatibility, docs). Read-only on the checkout; no sub-subagents; calibrate severity honestly.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                         |
| **receiving-code-review**                                    | "Technical evaluation, not emotional performance." Pattern: read → restate in your own words → verify against codebase reality → evaluate for *this* codebase → respond → implement one at a time. **Forbidden: "You're absolutely right!", "Great point!", any gratitude.** If any item is unclear, **stop and clarify all of them first** — partial understanding produces wrong implementation. External feedback: five checks before implementing; push back with technical reasoning; grep for actual usage before implementing a "professional" feature (YAGNI).                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                |
| **using-git-worktrees** / **finishing-a-development-branch** | Isolated worktree, clean verified baseline, never implement on main without explicit consent; at the end: verify tests → detect environment → confirm base branch → exactly three options → cleanup with provenance rules (only clean worktrees under `.worktrees/`; never `--force` on your own initiative). 10-row rationalization table.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                           |
| **dispatching-parallel-agents**                              | One agent per *independent problem domain*; multiple dispatches in **one response** = parallel, one per response = sequential. Don't use when failures are related or share state.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    |
| **writing-skills**                                           | **Writing skills IS TDD applied to process documentation**: pressure scenario = test case, skill = production code, agent violates the rule without the skill = RED, agent complies = GREEN, closing loopholes = REFACTOR. "If you didn't watch an agent fail without the skill, you don't know if the skill teaches the right thing." **The single most valuable empirical finding in either repo:** *a `description` must state only triggering conditions, never summarise the workflow* — a description reading "code review between tasks" caused agents to do ONE review when the skill's flowchart specified TWO; removing the workflow summary fixed it. "Descriptions that summarize workflow create a shortcut agents will take; the skill body becomes documentation agents skip." Plus SDO: keyword coverage (error strings, symptoms, synonyms), verb-first naming, and explicit token targets (<150 words for always-loaded, <500 otherwise).                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                           |

### Overall verdict

- **Copy Matt's architecture** (small composable skills, invocation split, router, vocabulary layers, `CONTEXT.md`, tracker-native task graphs, phase boundaries).
- **Copy Superpowers' execution machinery and enforcement content** (SDD controller, ledger, model tiers, artifact-as-file, plan Interfaces + Global Constraints, verification gate, the specific rationalization rows).
- **Keep your own domain depth** (Kafka/outbox/db-core/Spring standards) — that's your moat, and neither repo has anything comparable.
